target: Obat ini harus ditebus dengan resep dokter di apotek.
english: This medicine has to be filled with a doctor's prescription at the pharmacy.
grammar: Obat resep = prescription medicine: harus ditebus dengan resep = must be filled with a prescription.

target: Obat warung biasanya cukup untuk sakit kepala ringan seperti ini.
english: Corner-stall medicine is usually enough for a mild headache like this.
grammar: Obat warung = cheap over-the-counter meds from corner stalls, sold per strip — no resep needed.

target: Apoteker menjelaskan aturan pakai obat ini dengan sangat sabar.
english: The pharmacist explains this medicine's directions for use very patiently.

target: Sirup obat batuk ini harus dikocok dulu sebelum diminum.
english: This cough syrup has to be shaken first before being drunk.
grammar: Dulu after a verb = 'first': dikocok dulu sebelum diminum = shaken first before drinking.

target: Anak saya lebih suka obat sirup daripada tablet karena rasanya manis.
english: My child prefers syrup medicine to tablets because it tastes sweet.

target: Salep ini dioleskan tipis-tipis pada kulit yang gatal dua kali sehari.
english: This ointment is applied thinly on the itchy skin twice a day.
grammar: Doubling an adjective = 'in that manner': dioleskan tipis-tipis = spread on thinly.

target: Minum tablet ini sesudah makan supaya lambung kamu tidak perih.
english: Take this tablet after eating so your stomach doesn't sting.

target: Jangan melebihi dosis yang tertulis di kemasan obat itu.
english: Don't exceed the dose written on that medicine's packaging.

target: Apotek dekat rumah kami buka dua puluh empat jam setiap hari.
english: The pharmacy near our house is open twenty-four hours every day.

target: Saya perlu membeli vitamin dan obat tetes mata di apotek.
english: I need to buy vitamins and eye drops at the pharmacy.

target: Obat ini bisa membuat kamu mengantuk, jadi jangan menyetir setelah meminumnya.
english: This medicine can make you drowsy, so don't drive after taking it.

target: Kalau demamnya tidak turun dalam tiga hari, segera periksakan ke dokter.
english: If the fever doesn't go down in three days, have it checked by a doctor right away.
grammar: Periksakan = have it checked: periksakan ke dokter = take it to the doctor. The -kan asks it done.

target: Apoteker menyarankan obat generik karena harganya jauh lebih murah.
english: The pharmacist recommends the generic medicine because its price is much cheaper.
grammar: Obat generik = generic medicine, same content but cheaper: minta obat generik = ask for the generic.

target: Simpan sirup ini di kulkas setelah botolnya dibuka pertama kali.
english: Store this syrup in the fridge after the bottle is opened for the first time.

target: Ibu selalu menyimpan kotak obat kecil di lemari dapur untuk keadaan darurat.
english: Mom always keeps a small medicine box in the kitchen cupboard for emergencies.

target: Obat alergi ini hanya boleh diminum satu tablet per hari.
english: This allergy medicine may only be taken one tablet per day.

target: Saya lupa membawa resep, jadi apoteker tidak bisa memberikan obatnya.
english: I forgot to bring the prescription, so the pharmacist can't hand over the medicine.

target: Tolong tuliskan aturan pakai di label supaya nenek tidak bingung.
english: Please write the directions for use on the label so Grandma doesn't get confused.

target: Tolong panggil ambulans, ayah saya tiba-tiba jatuh pingsan di kamar mandi!
english: Please call an ambulance, my father suddenly fainted in the bathroom!
grammar: Tolong + verb = please (asking for help): tolong panggil ambulans = please call an ambulance.

target: Pasien kecelakaan itu langsung dibawa ke UGD rumah sakit terdekat.
english: That accident patient was taken straight to the ER of the nearest hospital.
grammar: UGD (Unit Gawat Darurat) = the ER; many hospitals label it IGD instead. Ke UGD = to the ER.

target: Perawat di IGD memeriksa tekanan darah dan denyut nadi saya.
english: The nurse in the ER checks my blood pressure and pulse.

target: Nomor darurat di Indonesia adalah seratus dua belas, mudah diingat.
english: The emergency number in Indonesia is one hundred twelve, easy to remember.
grammar: 112 is Indonesia's general emergency number: nomor darurat = emergency number.

target: Luka di dahinya cukup dalam sehingga harus dijahit lima jahitan.
english: The wound on his forehead is quite deep, so it has to be closed with five stitches.

target: Adik saya keracunan makanan laut dan muntah-muntah sepanjang malam.
english: My younger sibling got food poisoning from seafood and kept vomiting all night.

target: Dokter jaga memasang infus karena pasien itu kekurangan cairan.
english: The doctor on duty puts in an IV drip because that patient lacks fluids.

target: Jangan panik, tekan lukanya dengan kain bersih sampai pendarahan berhenti.
english: Don't panic, press the wound with a clean cloth until the bleeding stops.

target: Golongan darah saya O, jadi saya sering diminta mendonorkan darah.
english: My blood type is O, so I'm often asked to donate blood.

target: Kalau ada kebakaran, jangan memakai lift, turunlah lewat tangga darurat.
english: If there's a fire, don't use the elevator; go down via the emergency stairs.
grammar: -lah softens a command: turunlah lewat tangga = do go down the stairs.

target: Suami saya menelepon ambulans sambil menenangkan anak-anak yang ketakutan.
english: My husband calls the ambulance while calming the frightened children.

target: Petugas UGD bertanya obat apa saja yang sedang diminum pasien.
english: The ER staff asks what medicines the patient is currently taking.

target: Untung ada tetangga yang mengantar kami ke rumah sakit tengah malam.
english: Luckily there was a neighbor who drove us to the hospital in the middle of the night.
grammar: Untung at the start of a sentence = luckily: untung ada tetangga = luckily there was a neighbor.

target: Dia tersedak bakso, untung temannya tahu cara menolongnya.
english: He choked on a meatball; luckily his friend knew how to help him.

target: Sebelum ambulans datang, baringkan pasien dan longgarkan kerah bajunya.
english: Before the ambulance arrives, lay the patient down and loosen his shirt collar.

target: Kepalanya terbentur pintu mobil, sekarang dia merasa mual dan pusing.
english: His head hit the car door; now he feels nauseous and dizzy.

target: Adik menangis keras waktu disuntik di lengan kirinya.
english: My little sibling cries loudly when injected in his left arm.

target: Keluarga pasien menunggu dengan cemas di depan ruang operasi.
english: The patient's family waits anxiously in front of the operating room.

target: Sejak pagi saya merasa mual dan tidak nafsu makan sama sekali.
english: Since morning I have felt nauseous and have no appetite at all.

target: Nenek mengeluh sesak napas setiap kali naik tangga ke lantai dua.
english: Grandma complains of shortness of breath every time she climbs the stairs to the second floor.
grammar: Mengeluh = to complain (of): mengeluh sesak napas = complains of shortness of breath.

target: Saya alergi udang, wajah saya langsung bengkak sesudah memakannya.
english: I am allergic to shrimp; my face swells up right after eating it.

target: Kulit saya gatal dan muncul bintik merah setelah meminum obat baru itu.
english: My skin is itchy and red spots appeared after I took that new medicine.

target: Tenggorokan saya kering dan suara saya hampir hilang sejak kemarin.
english: My throat is dry and my voice has almost disappeared since yesterday.

target: Badan saya lemas dan kepala saya pusing seperti berputar.
english: My body is weak and my head is dizzy, like it's spinning.
grammar: Pusing covers both dizzy and stressed-out: kepala saya pusing = my head is spinning.

target: Anak itu demam tinggi dan menggigil meskipun sudah memakai selimut tebal.
english: That child has a high fever and is shivering even though he's already using a thick blanket.

target: Dokter bertanya sudah berapa lama saya merasakan nyeri di dada.
english: The doctor asks how long I have been feeling pain in my chest.

target: Perut saya kembung dan mulas setelah makan pedas semalam.
english: My stomach is bloated and crampy after eating spicy food last night.
grammar: Kembung = bloated, full of gas: perut kembung = a bloated belly.

target: Mata saya merah dan berair, mungkin karena debu di jalan.
english: My eyes are red and watery, maybe because of the dust on the road.

target: Dia batuk berdahak sudah seminggu, sebaiknya dia segera ke dokter.
english: He has had a phlegmy cough for a week already; he had better go to the doctor soon.

target: Telinga kanan saya berdenging sejak turun dari pesawat tadi malam.
english: My right ear has been ringing since I got off the plane last night.

target: Tekanan darah ayah naik lagi karena dia lupa meminum obatnya.
english: Dad's blood pressure went up again because he forgot to take his medicine.

target: Saya sulit tidur karena hidung tersumbat dan kepala terasa berat.
english: I have trouble sleeping because my nose is blocked and my head feels heavy.

target: Lutut saya bengkak setelah jatuh dari sepeda kemarin sore.
english: My knee is swollen after I fell off my bicycle yesterday afternoon.

target: Napasnya berbunyi seperti siulan, mungkin asmanya kambuh lagi.
english: His breathing sounds like whistling; maybe his asthma is flaring up again.
grammar: Kambuh = (an illness) flares up again: asmanya kambuh = his asthma is back.

target: Setiap musim hujan, alergi dingin saya kambuh dan kulit jadi gatal.
english: Every rainy season my cold allergy flares up and my skin gets itchy.

target: Dia mengalami mimisan tiba-tiba, mungkin karena cuaca terlalu panas.
english: He suddenly got a nosebleed, maybe because the weather is too hot.

target: Kartu BPJS saya tertinggal di rumah, untung ada versi digitalnya.
english: My BPJS card was left at home; luckily there is a digital version of it.
grammar: BPJS = Indonesia's national health insurance; nearly everyone carries the kartu BPJS = BPJS card.

target: Untuk berobat murah, warga biasanya datang dulu ke puskesmas dekat rumah.
english: For cheap medical treatment, residents usually go first to the puskesmas near their homes.
grammar: Puskesmas (pusat kesehatan masyarakat) = community health center, the cheap first stop for care.

target: Petugas puskesmas meminta saya mengambil nomor antrean di mesin.
english: The puskesmas staff asks me to take a queue number at the machine.

target: Tanpa surat rujukan dari puskesmas, BPJS tidak menanggung biaya rumah sakit.
english: Without a referral letter from the puskesmas, BPJS doesn't cover the hospital costs.
grammar: BPJS is tiered: you need a surat rujukan (referral letter) from the puskesmas before the hospital.

target: Ibu rutin memeriksakan gula darahnya di puskesmas setiap awal bulan.
english: Mom routinely has her blood sugar checked at the puskesmas at the start of every month.

target: Iuran BPJS keluarga kami dibayar otomatis lewat aplikasi bank.
english: Our family's BPJS premiums are paid automatically through the bank app.
grammar: Iuran = a regular membership fee: iuran BPJS = the monthly BPJS premium.

target: Antrean di puskesmas pagi ini panjang sekali sampai ke halaman.
english: The queue at the puskesmas this morning is really long, all the way to the yard.

target: Dokter puskesmas merujuk saya ke dokter spesialis kulit di rumah sakit.
english: The puskesmas doctor refers me to a skin specialist at the hospital.

target: Bidan di puskesmas memeriksa kandungan kakak saya setiap bulan.
english: The midwife at the puskesmas examines my older sister's pregnancy every month.

target: Anak-anak mendapat imunisasi gratis di posyandu dekat balai desa.
english: The children get free immunizations at the posyandu near the village hall.
grammar: Posyandu = neighborhood health post: monthly weigh-ins and shots for kids. Di posyandu = at the post.

target: Kelas BPJS menentukan jenis kamar rawat inap yang kamu dapat.
english: Your BPJS tier determines the type of inpatient room you get.

target: Saya harus memperbarui data alamat supaya kartu BPJS tetap aktif.
english: I have to update my address data so my BPJS card stays active.

target: Obat dari puskesmas gratis, kita hanya perlu menunjukkan kartu berobat.
english: Medicine from the puskesmas is free; we only need to show our patient card.

target: Puskesmas keliling datang ke kampung kami setiap hari Rabu pagi.
english: The mobile puskesmas comes to our neighborhood every Wednesday morning.

target: Pak RT membantu mengurus kartu BPJS untuk warga yang belum punya.
english: The neighborhood chief helps arrange BPJS cards for residents who don't have one yet.

target: Gigi geraham saya berlubang dan sakitnya menjalar sampai ke telinga.
english: My molar has a cavity and the pain spreads all the way to my ear.
grammar: Menjalar = (pain) spreads, creeps: sakitnya menjalar ke telinga = the pain spreads to the ear.

target: Dokter gigi menyarankan gigi itu ditambal sebelum lubangnya makin besar.
english: The dentist suggests that tooth be filled before the cavity gets bigger.

target: Anak saya takut sekali setiap kali diajak ke dokter gigi.
english: My child is really scared every time he is taken to the dentist.

target: Gigi bungsunya harus dicabut karena tumbuh miring dan menekan gigi lain.
english: His wisdom tooth has to be pulled because it grows crooked and presses on the other teeth.
grammar: Gigi bungsu = wisdom tooth, literally 'youngest-child tooth': dicabut = gets pulled.

target: Setelah gigi dicabut, jangan berkumur terlalu keras selama satu hari.
english: After the tooth is pulled, don't rinse your mouth too hard for one day.

target: Saya membersihkan karang gigi di klinik setiap enam bulan sekali.
english: I get my tartar cleaned at the clinic once every six months.

target: Adik memakai behel, jadi setiap bulan dia ke dokter gigi untuk kontrol.
english: My younger sibling wears braces, so every month she goes to the dentist for a checkup.

target: Gusi saya berdarah setiap kali menyikat gigi terlalu kencang.
english: My gums bleed every time I brush my teeth too hard.

target: Dokter gigi memuji anak saya karena rajin menggosok gigi sebelum tidur.
english: The dentist praises my child for diligently brushing his teeth before bed.

target: Biaya menambal satu gigi di klinik swasta lumayan mahal.
english: The cost of filling one tooth at a private clinic is pretty expensive.

target: Mata minus saya bertambah karena terlalu sering menatap layar ponsel.
english: My nearsightedness has gotten worse because I stare at my phone screen too often.
grammar: Mata minus = nearsighted, said with the number: minus saya bertambah = my prescription got worse.

target: Petugas optik memeriksa mata saya dengan mesin sebelum membuat kacamata.
english: The optician checks my eyes with a machine before making the glasses.

target: Kacamata baru ini membuat tulisan di papan terlihat jelas lagi.
english: These new glasses make the writing on the board look clear again.

target: Bingkai kacamata itu cocok dengan bentuk wajah kamu.
english: That glasses frame suits the shape of your face.

target: Ayah memakai kacamata baca setiap kali membuka koran pagi.
english: Dad puts on his reading glasses every time he opens the morning paper.
grammar: Kacamata = glasses, literally kaca (glass) + mata (eye): kacamata baca = reading glasses.

target: Lensa kontak lebih praktis untuk olahraga, tapi mata saya cepat kering.
english: Contact lenses are more practical for sports, but my eyes dry out quickly.

target: Kacamata saya patah karena diduduki adik kecil saya kemarin.
english: My glasses broke because my little sibling sat on them yesterday.

target: Di optik itu, kacamata bisa selesai dalam waktu satu jam saja.
english: At that optical shop, glasses can be finished in just one hour.

target: Ukuran minus mata kiri dan kanan saya ternyata berbeda jauh.
english: It turns out the prescriptions of my left and right eyes differ a lot.

target: Dokter mata menyarankan saya mengistirahatkan mata setiap dua puluh menit.
english: The eye doctor advises me to rest my eyes every twenty minutes.

target: Kalau badan pegal dan meriang, orang Indonesia bilang sedang masuk angin.
english: When the body is achy and feverish, Indonesians say you have 'masuk angin'.
grammar: Masuk angin ('wind got in') = the classic catch-all unwellness: chills, bloating, fatigue. Untranslatable.

target: Nenek minta dikerok punggungnya setiap kali merasa masuk angin.
english: Grandma asks to have her back coin-rubbed every time she feels she has masuk angin.
grammar: Kerokan: rubbing a coin down the back until it stripes red — the beloved home cure for masuk angin.

target: Bekas kerokan di punggung ayah merah semua, katanya makin merah makin manjur.
english: The kerokan marks on Dad's back are all red; he says the redder, the more effective.

target: Setiap pagi ibu minum jamu kunyit asam buatan tetangga.
english: Every morning Mom drinks turmeric-tamarind jamu made by the neighbor.
grammar: Jamu = traditional herbal tonic (turmeric, ginger...): minum jamu = drink jamu, for health not taste.

target: Penjual jamu gendong masih lewat depan rumah kami setiap pagi.
english: The traveling jamu seller still passes in front of our house every morning.
grammar: Jamu gendong = jamu sold by a walking vendor carrying bottles in a back sling (gendong = carry on the back).

target: Kata nenek, wedang jahe hangat ampuh untuk menghangatkan badan saat hujan.
english: According to Grandma, warm ginger drink works wonders for warming the body when it rains.

target: Ibu mengoleskan minyak kayu putih di perut adik yang kembung.
english: Mom rubs cajuput oil on my little sibling's bloated tummy.
grammar: Minyak kayu putih = cajuput oil, the warm-smelling cure-all rubbed on every Indonesian child's belly.

target: Tukang urut langganan keluarga kami datang ke rumah setiap bulan.
english: Our family's regular massage man comes to the house every month.

target: Setelah diurut, kaki saya yang keseleo terasa jauh lebih enak.
english: After being massaged, my sprained foot feels much better.

target: Banyak orang percaya bawang merah bisa menurunkan demam anak kecil.
english: Many people believe shallots can bring down a small child's fever.

target: Minum air kelapa muda katanya bagus untuk meredakan panas dalam.
english: Drinking young coconut water is said to be good for soothing 'panas dalam'.
grammar: Panas dalam ('inner heat') = folk ailment behind sore throats and canker sores; cooled with kelapa muda.

target: Sehabis melahirkan, kakak saya minum jamu supaya badannya cepat pulih.
english: After giving birth, my older sister drinks jamu so her body recovers quickly.

target: Campuran madu dan jeruk nipis jadi andalan ibu untuk meredakan batuk.
english: A mix of honey and lime is Mom's go-to for easing a cough.

target: Meskipun modern, dokter kami tidak melarang kerokan asal kulit tidak terluka.
english: Even though he is modern, our doctor doesn't forbid kerokan as long as the skin isn't injured.
grammar: Asal = as long as (condition): asal kulit tidak terluka = as long as the skin isn't hurt.

target: Balsam hangat ini selalu ada di dalam tas nenek ke mana-mana.
english: This warming balm is always in Grandma's bag wherever she goes.

target: Kantor saya menanggung asuransi kesehatan untuk karyawan dan keluarganya.
english: My office covers health insurance for the employees and their families.

target: Sebelum pulang, saya harus menyelesaikan tagihan rumah sakit di kasir.
english: Before going home, I have to settle the hospital bill at the cashier.

target: Jangan membuang kuitansi obat karena kita memerlukannya untuk klaim asuransi.
english: Don't throw away the medicine receipts because we need them for the insurance claim.
grammar: Kuitansi = official receipt (from Dutch 'kwitantie'): minta kuitansi = ask for a receipt.

target: Pihak asuransi menolak klaim kami karena satu dokumen kurang lengkap.
english: The insurance company rejected our claim because one document was incomplete.

target: Biaya rawat inap tiga hari itu hampir sepuluh juta rupiah.
english: The cost of that three-day hospital stay is almost ten million rupiah.

target: Untung asuransi kantor menanggung sebagian besar biaya operasi suami saya.
english: Luckily the office insurance covers most of the cost of my husband's operation.

target: Petugas administrasi menjelaskan rincian tagihan sebelum kami membayar.
english: The administration officer explains the breakdown of the bill before we pay.

target: Saya mencicil sisa tagihan rumah sakit selama enam bulan.
english: I am paying off the rest of the hospital bill in installments over six months.
grammar: Mencicil = pay in installments: mencicil tagihan = pay the bill bit by bit.

target: Simpan semua hasil laboratorium dan surat dokter untuk berkas klaim.
english: Keep all the lab results and doctor's letters for the claim file.

target: Asuransi perjalanan menanggung biaya berobat saya waktu sakit di Bali.
english: The travel insurance covered my treatment costs when I was sick in Bali.

target: Sore ini kami akan menjenguk paman yang dirawat di rumah sakit.
english: This afternoon we are going to visit our uncle who is hospitalized.
grammar: Menjenguk = visit someone sick or a new baby — a real social duty: menjenguk paman = visit uncle.

target: Teman-teman kantor patungan membeli parsel buah untuk menjenguk Bu Sari.
english: The office friends chip in to buy a fruit basket for visiting Mrs. Sari.
grammar: Patungan = chip in together: patungan membeli parsel = pool money to buy a gift basket.

target: Jangan lupa membawakan bubur ayam kesukaannya waktu menjenguk kakek nanti.
english: Don't forget to bring his favorite chicken porridge when visiting Grandpa later.

target: Semoga cepat sembuh, ya, kabari kami kalau perlu bantuan apa pun.
english: Get well soon, okay? Let us know if you need any help at all.
grammar: Semoga cepat sembuh = get well soon, literally 'hopefully quickly recover' — the standard sick wish.

target: Ibu menitip salam dan doa untuk tantemu yang sedang sakit.
english: Mom sends her greetings and prayers for your aunt who is sick.

target: Kami bergantian menjaga nenek di rumah sakit selama seminggu penuh.
english: We take turns watching over Grandma at the hospital for a full week.

target: Setelah operasi, pasien hanya boleh dijenguk oleh dua orang saja.
english: After the operation, the patient may only be visited by just two people.

target: Grup keluarga langsung ramai begitu kabar opname kakek tersebar.
english: The family group chat got lively as soon as news of Grandpa's hospitalization spread.
grammar: Opname (from Dutch) = being admitted to hospital: kabar opname kakek = news of Grandpa's hospital stay.

target: Tetangga datang membawa sup hangat waktu anak saya sakit demam berdarah.
english: The neighbors came bringing warm soup when my child was sick with dengue fever.
grammar: Demam berdarah (DBD) = dengue fever, literally 'bleeding fever' — the rainy-season worry.

target: Jenguklah dia selagi masih dirawat, dia pasti senang melihat kalian.
english: Do visit him while he is still hospitalized; he will surely be happy to see you all.

target: Sepulang dari rumah sakit, ayah dilarang bekerja berat selama sebulan.
english: After coming home from the hospital, Dad is forbidden from doing heavy work for a month.
